Σὺ μόνη χαῖρε, ἡ μήτηρ καὶ οὐρανός, ἡ κόρη καὶ νεφέλη, ἡ παρθένος καὶ
θρόνος· ὡς γὰρ μήτηρ ἔτεκες τὸν ἐκ σοῦ καὶ πρὸ σοῦ καὶ μετὰ σοῦ, ὡς δὲ παρθένος

συνέλαβες Λόγον καὶ ὤδινες μυστήριον, ὡς θρόνος ἐν γαστρὶ ἐβάστασας ὃν κατ'
οὐσίαν οὐ περιγράφει τις.
9 ∆ιὰ τοῦτο ὁ προφήτης Ἠσαΐας τὸ παρθενικὸν ἐκπληττόμενος μυστήριον
ἐβόα· «Φωνὴ κραυγῆς ἐκ πόλεως, φωνὴ κραυγῆς ἐκ ναοῦ» ἠκούσθη. Τί δὲ λέγεις, ὦ
προφῆτα; Ἀσφαλὲς τὸ αἴνιγμα καὶ βαθὺ τὸ νόημα. «Φωνὴ κραυγῆς ἐκ πόλεως, φωνὴ

ἐκ ναοῦ» ἠκούσθη· φωνὴν τὸν Ἰωάννην καλεῖ, κραυγὴν τὰ σκιρτήματα λέγει, πόλιν
τὴν Ἐλισάβετ ὀνομάζει, ναὸν τὸ σπήλαιον κηρύττει. «Φωνὴ κραυγῆς» ἠκούσθη
λέγουσα· «πρὶν τὴν ὠδίνουσαν τεκεῖν, πρὶν ἐλθεῖν τὸν πόνον τῶν ὠδίνων, ἐξέφυγε
καὶ ἔτεκεν ἄρ σεν.» Καὶ ἔλαβεν τοῦ μυστηρίου πάντα ὁμοῦ καὶ τάχος καὶ τόκον καὶ
παρθενίαν καὶ θαῦμα, ὅτι γὰρ οὐκ ἐκ μίξεως τὸ βρέφος. «Πρίν», φησίν, «ἐλθεῖν τὸν
πόνον τῶν ὠδίνων»· οὐκ ἔπαθε γὰρ τὰ τῆς Εὔας ἡ ἁγία Μαρία. «Ἐξέφυγε γὰρ καὶ
ἔτεκεν ἄρσεν»· οὐκ ἀνέμεινε φύσεως ὅρους ἡ χάρις· ἀπρόθεσμον γὰρ τὸ τῆς
οἰκονομίας μυστήριον. «Χαῖρε τοίνυν κεχαριτωμένη, ὁ κύριος μετὰ σοῦ»· ὁ γὰρ
κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τοὺς τῆς φιλοξενίας ἀνέῳξε κόλπους, ἀποστόλους
θαλαμεύει, εὐαγγελιστὰς τελειοῖ, ἐξ ὧν καὶ τὸν μακάριον Λουκᾶν ῥήτορα καὶ
διδάσκαλον τῆς ἐκκλησίας κατέστησεν.
10 Ἔστιν δὲ οὗτος ὁ τρισόλβιος εὐαγγελιστὴς Λουκᾶς Σύρος τὸ γένος, ἰατρὸς
τὴν τέχνην, μαθητὴς δὲ τῶν ἀποστόλων γενόμενος, καὶ ὕστερον Παύλῳ
παρακολουθήσας μέχρι τοῦ μαρτυρίου αὐτοῦ, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα δουλεύσας τῷ κυρίῳ
ἀπερισπάστως ἐκήρυξεν τὸν λόγον. Ἀρεταῖς παντοίαις κοσμούμενος καὶ χαρίσμασιν
θείοις διαλάμπων, ὀγδοήκοντα τεσσάρων ἐτῶν γενόμενος ἐκοιμήθη ἐν Θήβαις τῇ
μητροπόλει τῆς Βοιωτίας, πλήρης Πνεύματος ἁγίου. Οὗτος ἔγραψε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον
δηλῶν διὰ τοῦ προοιμίου τοῦτο ὅτι πρὸ αὐτοῦ ἄλλα ἐστὶ γεγραμμένα καὶ ὅτι
ἀναγκαῖον ἦν τοῖς ἐξ Ἑλλήνων πιστοῖς τὴν ἀκριβῆ τῆς οἰκονομίας ἐκθέσθαι
διήγησιν. Ἀνεπαύσατο δὲ ὁ ἅγιος Λουκᾶς ὁ εὐαγγελιστὴς μηνὶ ὀκτωβρίῳ
ὀκτωκαιδεκάτῃ, χάριτι τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος σὺν
τῷ ἀθανάτῳ Πατρὶ καὶ τῷ παναγίῳ καὶ ζωοποιῷ Πνεύματι, νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς
αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.

thought_title: Only the Virgin rejoices, and Luke rests in Thebes
orientation: Hesychius finishes his praise of Luke by reading Isaiah as prophecy of the virginal birth and then recounting Luke's origin, Gospel, and death.
pass_a_gloss: You alone rejoice, the mother and heaven, the maiden and cloud, the Virgin Mary and throne; for as mother you bore the one from you and before you and with you, and as the Virgin Mary you conceived the divine Word and labored with a mystery, and as throne in the womb you carried him whom in respect to essence no one circumscribes. On account of this the prophet Isaiah, struck with wonder at the virginal mystery, cried out: A voice of crying from the city, a voice of crying from the temple was heard. What do you say, O prophet? Secure is the riddle and deep is the meaning. A voice of crying from the city, a voice from the temple was heard; voice he calls John, cry he says are the leapings, city he names Elizabeth, temple he proclaims to be the cave. A voice of crying was heard saying: Before the woman in labor bore, before the pain of the pains of giving birth came, she escaped and bore a male. And he received of the mystery all things together both swiftness and birth and virginity and wonder, for the infant is not from mingling. Before, he says, the pain of the pains of giving birth came; for holy Mary did not suffer the things of Eve. For she escaped and bore a male; for grace did not wait for the bounds of nature; for the mystery of the plan of salvation is without appointed time. Rejoice therefore, favored one, the Lord is with you; for our Lord Jesus Christ opened the folds of hospitality, he brings apostles into the bridal chamber, he brings evangelists to completion, from among whom he also established the blessed Luke as speaker and teacher of the church. And this three times blessed evangelist Luke is Syrian by birth, physician by craft, having become a disciple of the apostles, and later having accompanied Paul until his martyrdom, and after these things having served the Lord without distraction he proclaimed the word. Adorned with virtues of every kind and shining with divine gifts, having become eighty four years old he fell asleep in Thebes the chief city of Boeotia, full of Holy Spirit. This one wrote the Gospel, showing through the preface this, that before him other things stand written and that it was necessary to set forth for the believers from the Greeks the exact narrative of the plan of salvation. And Saint Luke the evangelist rested on the eighteenth of the month of October, by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom is the glory and the might with the deathless Father and the most holy Spirit who gives life, now and always and unto the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.term: ὡς θρόνος ἐν γαστρὶ ἐβάστασας ὃν κατ᾽ οὐσίαν οὐ περιγράφει τις
choices.english: as throne in the womb you carried him whom in respect to essence no one circumscribes
choices.why: keeps throne image and the essence qualifier literal rather than paraphrasing as infinity

choices.english: he brings apostles into the bridal chamber
choices.why: verb comes from bridal chamber and means leading in, not storing; context is honor and union
rejected: he stores up apostles in his chambers

choices.term: ἔλαβεν τοῦ μυστηρίου πάντα ὁμοῦ καὶ τάχος καὶ τόκον καὶ παρθενίαν καὶ θαῦμα
choices.english: he received of the mystery all things together both swiftness and birth and virginity and wonder
choices.why: together with swiftness stresses the sudden painless birth, not merely manner

choices.term: ἀπρόθεσμον γὰρ τὸ τῆς οἰκονομίας μυστήριον
choices.english: the mystery of the plan of salvation is without appointed time
choices.why: uses glossary for plan of salvation and keeps negation of fixed deadline, explaining grace not waiting for nature

pass_b_english: You alone rejoice, mother and heaven, maiden and cloud, the Virgin Mary and throne. As mother you bore the one who is from you and before you and with you. As the Virgin Mary you conceived the divine Word and labored to bring forth a mystery. As throne you carried in the womb him whom no one limits in his essence.

For this reason the prophet Isaiah stood in awe at the virginal mystery and cried out, “A voice of crying from the city, a voice from the temple was heard” (Isaiah 66:6). But what are you saying, O prophet? The riddle is firm and its meaning is deep. Isaiah calls John the voice, and he means the leaping in the womb by the cry. He names Elizabeth the city, and he proclaims the cave the temple. A voice of crying was heard saying, “Before she who was in labor gave birth, before the pain of labor came, she escaped and bore a male child” (Isaiah 66:7). The prophet took in the whole mystery at once, its swiftness and its birth and its virginity and its wonder, for the child came from no union. Isaiah says, “Before the pain of labor came,” for holy Mary did not suffer what Eve suffered. Isaiah says, “She escaped and bore a male child,” for grace did not wait for the limits of nature. The mystery of the plan of salvation keeps no set date.

So then, “Rejoice, favored one, the Lord is with you” (Luke 1:28). For our Lord Jesus Christ has opened the arms of his welcome. He brings apostles into the bridal chamber, and he brings evangelists to completion. From them he established blessed Luke as speaker and teacher of the church.

This thrice-blessed evangelist Luke was Syrian by birth and physician by craft. He became a disciple of the apostles, and later he accompanied Paul until Paul’s martyrdom. After that he served the Lord without distraction and preached the word. Adorned with every virtue and shining with divine gifts, he fell asleep at eighty-four years of age in Thebes, the chief city of Boeotia, full of the Holy Spirit. He wrote the Gospel, showing through his preface that other accounts had been written before him and that believers from the Greeks needed an exact narrative of the plan of salvation set out for them. The holy evangelist Luke came to his rest on the eighteenth of October, by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom belong glory and might, together with the immortal Father and the all-holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
notes: Section numbers 9 and 10 and page number 3 in the source are not translated.

problems.quote: Hesychius says Isaiah calls John the voice
problems.why: Hesychius is the homilist speaking directly; inserting 'Hesychius says' falsely shifts his own voice into a third-person summary not in the source.
problems.ruling: Greek homily speaks directly (καλεῖ, λέγει, ὀνομάζει); no Ἡσύχιος. 'Hesychius says' adds a third-person frame that misleads.

edits.old: Hesychius says Isaiah calls John the voice

fixed: speaker: removed 'Hesychius says' — source φωνὴν τὸν Ἰωάννην καλεῖ has Isaiah as subject speaking in Hesychius's own voice; English now reads 'Isaiah calls John the voice'.
